script.text: The U.S. says the Iran war is over. So why is Hormuz still shut?

On Monday, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, President Trump said the Iran war is militarily effectively over. He said the U.S. is keeping the status quo and holding off new strikes. Al Jazeera notes that means sanctions continue. But CBS reports he also warned American forces are locked and loaded.

The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports stays in place. Reuters reports Iran's proposal would halt U.S. bombing, ease sanctions and end the blockade of Iranian ports, in return for reopening Hormuz, with nuclear talks to follow.

Iran's foreign ministry says it will keep its commitments if Washington lifts the blockade and sanctions. Security official Mohsen Rezaei demands the U.S. accept Iran's seven conditions. Qatar says talks continue.
Will Hormuz reopen before December? Yes or no?

upload.title: US Says Iran War Is Over. Why Is Hormuz Still Shut? #shorts
upload.description:
On Monday, November 9, after meeting Qatar's prime minister in Washington, President Donald Trump said the war with Iran is "militarily effectively over" and that the U.S. is keeping the "status quo" while holding off new strikes. CBS News reports he also said the American military is "locked and loaded". The U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in effect. According to Reuters, Iran's proposal would halt U.S. bombing, ease sanctions and end the blockade of Iranian ports in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with nuclear negotiations to follow. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran would meet its commitments if Washington lifts sanctions and the blockade. Security official Mohsen Rezaei demanded that the U.S. accept Iran's seven conditions and dismissed reports of ongoing negotiations. Qatar said talks continue in close coordination with both sides. Most details come from officials and the parties themselves and could not be independently verified.
